text:
Alex W: Heads-up — we got an odd burst on hosted generation around 09:12 UTC. Reserved pools dipped below target for ~18m and cloud billing shows a spike in on-demand GPU costs. Can someone triage the demand spill pattern?

Maria S: saw the alert. digging in now, looks like a mix of long-seq batch jobs + a few high-QPS customers. attaching quick snapshot.

Maria S: usage peek: hosted-pool-eu: committed 320 GPUs, active 372 GPUs at peak, 15% on-demand fallback. cost delta ~ $6.2k for the window.

Sam R: yikes. any autocapacity rules hit? sounds like burst-stage > reserved threshold.

Jia L: autoscale logs show burst windows triggered but throttled by max-instant-burst = 40. a lot of requests were long context > 8k tokens which inflated GPU-time.

Ben T: is that the embed-heavy customer we saw last week? they switched to longer prompts via the new SDK.

Maria S: yes, customer-id: cust-78f, started a batch rerank job. 75% of extra load traced to them. also some smaller noise from retries during 09:10-09:20.

Alex W: Ops question: do we buy more reserved for eu to smooth Q2 forecast, or throttle/police at infra layer? need short-term mitigation and medium-term commit decision.

Sam R: short-term: (1) route non-latency jobs to dedicated-reserved-queue with lower priority, (2) apply temp rate-limit to any single API key > 12 rps for 10m. both quick.

Jia L: implementation for routing: add header X-inference-priority: low for jobs with max_latency > 500ms. quick patch:

```
# nginx map snippet
map $http_x_inference_priority $upstream {
  "low" backend-dedicated;
  default backend-hosted;
}
```

Ben T: medium-term: re-evaluate committed sizing. our 320 units assume average seq len 2k. if median drifts to 4k we underprovision. propose a sensitivity matrix and a 6-week runway buy option for incremental reservations.

Maria S: finance flagged we can do a 3-month add-on at ~7% discount vs on-demand. need exact hours/day impact to justify.

Alex W: action items: Maria — produce a 6-week sensitivity with cost delta and delta-per-commitment tier. Sam/Jia — implement routing+rate limits today as emergency mitigation. Ben — draft a recommendation for 3mo add-on vs throttling. OpsBot, log the incident for postmortem.

OpsBot: Incident created: #INC-2026-2219 | category: capacity_spill | severity: medium | assigned: eng-infra. Patch link: https://internal.redwood/inc/INC-2026-2219

Maria S: quick numbers I'll post in 10m. preliminary: shifting 20% of peak to dedicated would cut on-demand spend by ~$4.1k and reduce committed breach from 15% to ~4%.

Sam R: testing the route change now in staging, will push to prod in 8m if green.

Jia L: also flagged a network egress latched retry pattern — a couple of retries created amplification. adding jitter to retry backoff in SDK to avoid thundering herd. snippet: `retry_backoff = jittered_exponential(100ms, 2s)`

Ben T: for the commitment decision: if median seq stays at 3.5k+, a 5% commit increase buys ~18% lower unit cost vs current on-demand; I'll model weekly sensitivity and include a breakpoint for auto-buy threshold.

Alex W: good. once Maria posts exact numbers we'll convene a 15m sync to decide whether to purchase the 3mo add-on or rely on routing/limits. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Maria S: posting the sensitivity table now:

```
# sensitivity (peak scenario)
median_seq | committed_needed | est_on_demand_cost_delta
2k        | 320              | baseline
3k        | 360              | +$3.9k/week
4k        | 400              | +$8.7k/week
```

Maria S: recommending interim 40 GPU add-on for 3 months to buy runway while we tune batching/kv-cache. net projected savings vs on-demand: ~$32k over 3 months.

Sam R: rolling routing patch in 2m. will monitor errors/latency.

Jia L: SDK PR open to reduce retry amplification, will merge after 1 review.

Ben T: I'll draft the add-on PO and run it past finance. if they greenlight, we can lock by EOD.

Alex W: meeting in 15 to decide on add-on. thanks all.

Ben T: :rocket:
